+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Copyright 2026 The Stargate Authors
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# T155 Acceptance 4: the live-e2e tracker must exist, carry the required
+# sections, name only commands that exist, track the real-browser Direct-fallback
+# probe and the release-cadence checks, and never record an unrun check as PASS
+# (Constitution VII: SKIP is not PASS; workflow.md "Live end-to-end verification").
+set -euo pipefail
+python3 - "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" <<'PY'
+import re
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+root = Path(sys.argv[1])
+readme = root / 'specs/001-tor-route/live-e2e/README.md'
+errors = []
+
+if not readme.is_file():
+    print('FAIL: specs/001-tor-route/live-e2e/README.md is missing (T155 Acceptance 4)',
+          file=sys.stderr)
+    sys.exit(1)
+text = readme.read_text()
+
+
+def need(label, pattern, flags=re.I | re.S):
+    if not re.search(pattern, text, flags):
+        errors.append(f'missing: {label}')
+
+
+# Required content named by Acceptance 4.
+need('prerequisites section', r'^## .*environment.*disposable host', re.I | re.M)
+need('foundation checks table', r'^## 1\. Foundation checks', re.I | re.M)
+need('evidence index with a snapshot hash',
+     r'## Evidence index.*snapshot\.\*\*\s+executable content is commit `[0-9a-f]{40}`')
+need('preserve/reset semantics', r'### Preserve / reset.*reset every run.*preserve across runs')
+need('transport-relevant vs invisible classification',
+     r'transport-relevant \(live only\).*transport-invisible \(stays in contract tests\)')
+need('real-browser hardening/token-failure probe with packet attribution',
+     r'real-browser hardening / token-failure probe.*direct fallback.*packet attribution')
+need('SKIP is never PASS rule', r'never recorded as pass|never pass', re.I)
+for ticket in ('T186', 'T188', 'T034a', 'T034f', 'T070a'):
+    need(f'{ticket} named', rf'\b{ticket}\b')
+need('browser launch / session restore obligation',
+     r'browser launch and session restore.*run before every release')
+# The evidence snapshot must name a real commit, not any 40-hex string.
+snap = re.search(r'executable content is commit `([0-9a-f]{40})`', text, re.I)
+if snap and subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(root), 'cat-file', '-e', snap.group(1) + '^{commit}'],
+                           capture_output=True).returncode != 0:
+    errors.append(f'evidence snapshot {snap.group(1)} is not a commit in this repository')
+decisions = set(re.findall(r'\*\*D-live-(\d+)', text))
+if len(decisions) < 3:
+    errors.append(f'D-live-N decisions log needs at least 3 entries, found {len(decisions)}')
+
+# Every repository path the tracker tells an operator to run must exist.
+for path in sorted(set(re.findall(
+        r'(?:tests/(?:live-e2e|contract|integration)/[\w./-]+\.(?:py|sh|go)|extension/package\.sh|scripts/verify\.sh)',
+        text))):
+    if not (root / path).is_file():
+        errors.append(f'command path does not exist: {path}')
+
+# An unrun release-cadence check must not carry a PASS status, and a check
+# definition row (F-n) is not a result. An R-n row may name PASS only in the
+# exact negation "never recorded as PASS"; any other PASS/PASSED/GREEN/OK, or a
+# "passed"/"green" in any case, in an R-n or F-n row is an error (a nearby "not"
+# elsewhere in the row is no excuse). Lower-case "pass" stays usable as a noun.
+for line in text.splitlines():
+    if not re.match(r'\|\s*[RF]-?\d+\s*\|', line):
+        continue
+    rest = line.replace('never recorded as PASS', '')
+    if re.search(r'\b(PASS|OK)\b', rest) or re.search(r'\b(passed|green)\b', rest, re.I):
+        errors.append(f'check row claims a result: {line[:80]}')
+
+if errors:
+    print('FAIL: live-e2e tracker (T155 Acceptance 4):', file=sys.stderr)
+    for e in errors:
+        print(f'  - {e}', file=sys.stderr)
+    sys.exit(1)
+print('OK: live-e2e tracker sections, commands, probe tracking and no unrun PASS')
+PY

+// first-party-site axes of the isolation partition (spec FR-002;
+// Constitution III stream isolation; contracts/foundation-boundaries.md).
+// T126 varies only the browser-profile axis. The partition username is
+// HMAC-SHA-256 keyed by the device's bearer token over the tuple
+// (profile, context, site), so two devices (two tokens) or two first-party
+// sites reaching ONE destination must also land on distinct Tor circuits.
+//
+// The live subtests run inside TestStreamIsolationDPUNAMEForwarding's stack
+// (same bring-up, same calibration): each axis pair holds one axis different
+// and everything else (target, profile, context) equal, and the pair must
+// attach to distinct, non-zero, BUILT circuits. The calibration there (one
+// partition twice shares one circuit) is what makes a green result
+// meaningful: a data plane that fused, dropped or constant-folded the
+// upstream username collapses every pair onto one circuit and fails them.
+//
+// The hermetic test below pins the derivation of each axis to independently
+// computed vectors (Python hmac/hashlib over the same JSON tuple), so a
+// drift that stops an axis from changing the username fails in the PR gate.

+)

+
+// TestT155PartitionAxesDerivation pins each axis to an independent vector.
+func TestT155PartitionAxesDerivation(t *testing.T) {
+	const token = "0f1e2d3c0f1e2d3c0f1e2d3c0f1e2d3c"
+	profile := strings.Repeat("11", 32)
+	onion := strings.Repeat("abcd2345", 7) + ".onion"
+	vectors := []struct {
+		name, got, want string
+	}{
+		{"base (foundation-boundaries reference)", t126PartitionUsername(token, profile, onion),
+			"sg1:1940cde7068246610f120ee0926ad88113942aa2e83d71ba649deab843077a06"},
+		{"device axis (other token)", t126PartitionUsername(t155DeviceTwoToken, profile, onion),
+			"sg1:fb949c3678076ecb821ae348014b63e26545145dcb8a92ac4c505ddfb5c82f3d"},
+		{"site axis (other first-party site)", t126PartitionUsername(token, profile, t155SiteTwoOnion),

+		{"profile axis (other profile)", t126PartitionUsername(token, strings.Repeat("22", 32), onion),
+			"sg1:625891e4088b29c3c9134a12055b82d13b63ddc7f9156b47156f8fb74e94c2ac"},
+	}
+	seen := map[string]string{}
+	for _, v := range vectors {
+		if v.got != v.want {

+		if prior, dup := seen[v.got]; dup {

+// t155RunAxisPair drains the target's streams, dials base and variant in
+// parallel through the DP, and requires distinct, non-zero, BUILT circuits.
+// The pair differs on exactly one axis, named for the failure message.
+func t155RunAxisPair(t *testing.T, ctx context.Context, ctl t126ControlFn, composeFile, envFile, target, axis string,
+	base, variant t155Cred, forensics func() string) {
+	t.Helper()
+	if base.user == variant.user {
+		t.Fatalf("%s axis pair has identical usernames — the pair would not test isolation", axis)
+	}
+	if _, err := t126WaitStreams(ctx, ctl, target, 0, t126DrainWait); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("drain before %s pair: %v\n%s", axis, err, forensics())
+	}
+	c0, c1 := t155ParallelConnect(t, ctx, composeFile, envFile, base, variant, t126ConnectWait)
+	defer c0.Close()
+	defer c1.Close()
+	circ, err := t126WaitStreams(ctx, ctl, target, 2, t126StreamWait)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("%v\n%s", err, forensics())
+	}
+	if circ[0] == "0" || circ[1] == "0" {
+		t.Fatalf("%s axis: stream(s) reported unattached (CircID 0): %v\n%s", axis, circ, forensics())
+	}
+	if circ[0] == circ[1] {
+		t.Fatalf("ISOLATION: partitions differing only in the %s axis shared circuit %s to the same target through %s — "+
+			"the upstream SOCKS5 username was fused, dropped or constant-folded (FR-007/FR-002)\n%s",
+			axis, circ[0], t126DPAddr, forensics())
+	}
+	for _, id := range circ {
+		built, err := t126CircuitBuilt(ctx, ctl, id)
+		if err != nil || !built {
+			t.Errorf("%s axis: circuit %s not found BUILT (err: %v)\n%s", axis, id, err, forensics())
+		}
+	}
+	t.Logf("OK: %s axis → distinct circuits %s / %s, both BUILT", axis, circ[0], circ[1])
+}
+
+// t155ParallelConnect is t126ParallelConnect with a token per identity (the
+// device axis needs two bearers). Same starting gun, per-dial retry window and
+// forensics.
+func t155ParallelConnect(t *testing.T, ctx context.Context, composeFile, envFile string, c0, c1 t155Cred, wait time.Duration) (net.Conn, net.Conn) {
+	t.Helper()
+	type result struct {
+		idx  int
+		conn net.Conn
+		err  error
+	}
+	start := make(chan struct{})
+	results := make(chan result, 2)
+	for i, cred := range []t155Cred{c0, c1} {
+		go func(idx int, cred t155Cred) {
+			<-start
+			wCtx, wCancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, wait)
+			defer wCancel()
+			for {
+				conn, err := t126Connect(wCtx, cred.user, cred.token)
+				if err == nil {
+					results <- result{idx: idx, conn: conn}
+					return
+				}
+				if wCtx.Err() != nil {
+					results <- result{idx: idx, err: err}
+					return
+				}
+				time.Sleep(t126StreamPoll)
+			}
+		}(i, cred)
+	}
+	close(start)
+	var conns [2]net.Conn
+	var errs [2]error
+	for n := 0; n < 2; n++ {
+		r := <-results
+		conns[r.idx], errs[r.idx] = r.conn, r.err
+	}
+	if errs[0] != nil || errs[1] != nil {
+		for _, c := range conns {
+			if c != nil {
+				_ = c.Close()
+			}
+		}
+		t.Fatalf("parallel CONNECT through %s did not establish both streams within %s\n  #0: %s\n  #1: %s\n%s\n%s",
+			t126DPAddr, wait, t059ClassifyDialErr(errs[0]), t059ClassifyDialErr(errs[1]),
+			t126LogTail(ctx, composeFile, envFile, "stargate-dp", 12),
+			t126LogTail(ctx, composeFile, envFile, "tor", 15))
+	}
+	return conns[0], conns[1]
+}

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+# Copyright 2026 The Stargate Authors
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# T155 — stack phase on the disposable QEMU guest (run as root from the candidate
+# tree). Real `scripts/stargate init` on fresh volumes, then the quickstart
+# operator surface (tokens.yaml + `restart stargate-control` +
+# `scripts/stargate status`) drives Acceptance 2/7 checks against the deployed
+# DP on 127.0.0.1:8881. Synthetic tokens only; nothing secret is printed.
+# Every check is recorded PASS/FAIL; the script exits non-zero on any FAIL.
+#
+# `--only resumption` runs init, the first acknowledged reload and the TLS
+# resumption phase alone (the T155 tests-first probe); the default runs all.
+import hashlib
+import json
+import os
+import secrets
+import shutil
+import socket
+import sqlite3
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import time

+def await_status(rc, needle, timeout):
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
+    while True:
+        code, out = status()
+        if code == rc and needle in out[0]:

+        if time.monotonic() > deadline:

+        time.sleep(5)

+def recv_exact(conn, n):
+    data = b""
+    while len(data) < n:
+        part = conn.recv(n - len(data))
+        if not part:
+            break
+        data += part
+    return data

+def socks_auth(token, site=b"t155-device-profile-normal-example.com"):
+    """Return (state, conn): state is 'ok', 'denied' or 'closed'."""
+    conn = socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", 8881), timeout=10)
+    conn.settimeout(30)
+    conn.sendall(b"\x05\x01\x02")
+    if recv_exact(conn, 2) != b"\x05\x02":
+        conn.close()
+        return "closed", None
+    user = b"sg1:" + hashlib.sha256(site).hexdigest().encode()
+    t = token.encode()
+    conn.sendall(b"\x01" + bytes([len(user)]) + user + bytes([len(t)]) + t)
+    reply = recv_exact(conn, 2)
+    if reply == b"\x01\x00":
+        return "ok", conn
+    conn.close()
+    return ("denied" if reply == b"\x01\xff" else "closed"), None
+

+def auth_state(label):
+    try:
+        state, conn = socks_auth(TOK[label])
+        if conn:
+            conn.close()
+        return state
+    except OSError as exc:
+        return f"error:{type(exc).__name__}"

+def tor_bytes(label):
+    for attempt in range(3):
+        try:
+            state, conn = socks_auth(TOK[label])
+            if state != "ok":
+                return f"auth {state}"
+            with conn:
+                target = b"example.com"
+                conn.sendall(b"\x05\x01\x00\x03" + bytes([len(target)]) + target + b"\x00\x50")
+                rep = recv_exact(conn, 10)
+                if rep[:2] != b"\x05\x00":
+                    last = f"reply {rep[:2].hex()}"
+                    continue
+                conn.sendall(b"HEAD / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: example.com\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n")
+                head = conn.recv(64)
+                if head.startswith(b"HTTP/"):
+                    return "ok"
+                last = "no HTTP bytes"
+        except OSError as exc:
+            last = f"{type(exc).__name__}"
+        time.sleep(10)
+    return last

+def wait_listener(timeout=180):
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
+    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
+        try:
+            with socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", 8881), timeout=3) as c:
+                c.sendall(b"\x05\x01\x02")
+                if recv_exact(c, 2) == b"\x05\x02":
+                    return True
+        except OSError:
+            pass
+        time.sleep(2)
+    return False

+def resumption_phase():
+    """A2 peer-pin rotation/resumption. With the CP stopped (wire-auth.md §6.2
+    rotation order), `wireprobe resume`, as the CP identity, takes a session
+    ticket from the running DP, resumes it (positive control), rotates
+    cp.priv/cp.pub, offers the old ticket, then the old identity in a full
+    handshake, then the rotated identity. Its exit code decides; each step is
+    also recorded so a failure names its step. Afterwards the observer's
+    cp.pub copy is refreshed with init's helper and the CP restarts on the
+    rotated key."""
+    build_probe()
+    dp_id = run(C + ["ps", "-q", "stargate-dp"]).stdout.strip()
+
+    def dp_started():
+        return run(["docker", "inspect", "-f", "{{.State.StartedAt}} {{.State.Pid}}", dp_id]).stdout.strip()
+
+    run(C + ["stop", "stargate-control"])
+    started = dp_started()
+    r = subprocess.run(["docker", "run", "--rm", "--user", "5101:5100", "-v", f"{P}_stargate-ipc:/run/stargate",
+                        "-v", f"{P}_stargate-keys:/etc/stargate/keys", "-v", f"{ROOT}:/src", "-w", "/src", GIMG,
+                        "/src/target/stargate-wireprobe", "resume", "-socket", "/run/stargate/dp.sock"],
+                       capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=600)
+    (EV / "resume.log").write_text(r.stdout + r.stderr)
+    # The ticket must meet the same DP process that issued it.
+    check("DP process unchanged across the resumption probe", dp_started() == started, started)
+    steps = {l.split()[2].rstrip(":"): l for l in r.stdout.splitlines() if l.startswith("wireprobe: resume ")}
+
+    def step(name, *needles):
+        line = steps.get(name, "")
+        return bool(line) and all(n in line for n in needles), line.split(": ", 2)[-1] if line else "step not reached"
+
+    ok, d = step("2-old-resumed-before-rotation", "ticket_offered=true", "resumed=true", "rpc=answered")
+    check("resumption positive control: DP resumed the offered ticket before rotation", ok, d)
+    ok, d = step("4-old-ticket-after-rotation", "ticket_offered=true", "rpc=refused")
+    ok = ok and "first_handshake=[resumed=false]" not in d  # a declined ticket is not the resumed path
+    check("old CP identity offering its pre-rotation ticket gets no RPC answered", ok, d)
+    ok, d = step("5-old-full-after-rotation", "rpc=refused")
+    check("old CP identity refused on a full handshake after rotation", ok, d)
+    ok, d = step("6-rotated-full", "rpc=answered")
+    check("rotated CP identity answered (DP re-read the pin; the refusals are not an outage)", ok, d)
+    check("wireprobe resume exit 0", r.returncode == 0, f"exit {r.returncode} {r.stderr.strip()[-300:]}")

+    run(["docker", "run", "--rm", "--user", "0:0", "-v", f"{P}_stargate-keys:/etc/stargate/keys", GIMG, "bash", "-c",

+    run(["bash", "-c", '. scripts/lib/compose.sh && refresh_observer_cp_pub "$1" "$2"', "refresh",
+         f"{P}_stargate-keys", f"{P}_stargate-observer-keys"])
+    run(C + ["start", "stargate-control"])
+    s = await_status(0, "ACKNOWLEDGED(", 1200)
+    check("CP restarted on the rotated key: token delivery acknowledged", "ACKNOWLEDGED(" in s, s)

+# Live end-to-end tracker — 001-tor-route
+
+Single place for the release-cadence and foundation live checks the contract
+tests (`tests/contract/`) structurally cannot see: real Tor, the real deployed
+Compose stack, real kernel packet paths, and the real browser's proxy
+decisions. Form per `docs/process/workflow.md` §"Live end-to-end
+verification". Owner of the foundation checks: T155 (this file is its Acceptance
+4 deliverable). Raw artefacts stay under gitignored `target/`; nothing here
+contains a token, key, address or packet payload.
+
+**Rules.** A check that did not run is `NOT RUN`, a check that skipped is
+`SKIP`; neither is ever recorded as PASS. Every result binds the candidate
+snapshot it ran on and is invalidated by a later executable change to code,
+Compose, extension, image inputs or the harness itself. Live Tor-network
+checks use synthetic tokens and keys only.
+
+## 1. Foundation checks (T155)
+
+Candidate snapshot, host and evidence for the last complete pass are in the
+*Evidence index* at the end of this file. Commands run from the repository root
+of the exact candidate.

+### Preserve / reset
+
+- **Reset every run:** the Compose project and its volumes (`down --volumes`),
+  `tokens.yaml`, CP SQLite state, DP `dp-snapshot.json`, the generated keys
+  and pepper, and the browser profile (always a fresh ephemeral directory).
+  `run.py` (F1) refuses a pre-existing `stargate-dp` AppArmor profile or owner
+  rule and removes what it installs. F2 and F4 do not: `scripts/stargate
+  init` and the test provisioning leave the profile, the UID-5102 owner rules,
+  locally built and retagged images and, after a failed F2 run, its `/root`
+  state backups on the host. That is why the host is disposable, F1 runs first
+  on a freshly booted guest, and a rerun of F1 needs a reset or a reboot.
+- **Preserve across runs:** only the VM base image and the pinned browser/driver
+  archives. The DP cold-start cache (`dp-snapshot.json`, `data-model.md` §1.4)
+  is *not* a live-test artefact: F2 deliberately exercises it within one run
+  (restart restores the last acknowledged generation; a rolled-back CP set is
+  refused) and discards it with the volumes.
+- **Browser hardening state** is the exception for the separate release-cadence
+  profile check (section 4, R-6): the verified pref state is carried until the
+  next release run, `storage.local` audit result is reset.
+
+### Transport-relevant versus transport-invisible
+
+- **Transport-relevant (live only):** real Tor reachability and circuit
+  isolation, packet-level DP egress denial and its positive controls, CP
+  namespace absence of raw Tor control, real DNS resolver behaviour, deployed
+  init/provisioning, container restart/ordering behaviour, the real browser's
+  proxy decisions (Direct fallback, private windows, cache, startup order).
+- **Transport-invisible (stays in contract tests):** SOCKS5 byte sequences,
+  error-template literals, proto schema, token-file parsing, HMAC/pin logic in
+  isolation, aggregate bucket arithmetic, request-label derivation.
+
+## 2. Environment: disposable host (VM)
+
+The Local topology needs the `stargate-dp` AppArmor profile and owner iptables
+rules, so the checks run only on a disposable Linux Docker host with root,
+AppArmor, Landlock ABI >= 4, seccomp TSYNC, `tcpdump`, `ip`, `ss`, `strace`,
+IPv4/IPv6 iptables and Go. An independently booted QEMU guest (own kernel and
+namespaces) is the approved host; record whether the host is a VM. Procedure
+used for the foundation pass: boot the saved guest image from a per-ticket
+copy, ship the candidate's tracked and staged files as one tar and record its
+SHA-256 with the changed-file hashes, commit that tree to a throwaway
+repository in the guest (`run.py`'s observer helper records `git rev-parse
+HEAD`, which is then that local commit, not a project commit), compile the
+integration test binary on the host with the guest source path mapped, and run
+the phases in order. `run.py` refuses a host that already carries the
+`stargate-dp` profile or owner rules, so it runs first on a freshly booted
+guest. Delete the per-ticket guest copy and stop the VM afterwards.
+
+## 3. Real-browser probes (host)
+
+The reference browser is Mullvad Browser; the extension refuses a browser older
+than Gecko 153 (`minVersion` 153.0). The distribution's `/usr/bin/mullvad-browser`
+may be older and is not used. Use a pinned Mullvad Browser (the foundation pass
+used 153.3.0esr extracted under `target/t157-tools`) with geckodriver; probes use
+disposable ephemeral profiles and bind only host loopback listeners (8881 among
+them), so **do not run anything else that binds those ports or launches
+browsers while they run**.
+
+```sh
+bash extension/package.sh
+for m in descriptor-matrix blocked-proxy private-access full; do
+  python3 tests/live-e2e/mullvad-browser-hardening/probe.py \
+    --browser <pinned>/Browser/mullvadbrowser --driver <geckodriver> \
+    --extension extension/dist/stargate-extension.zip --only $m \
+    --report-out target/runs/<run>/$m.json
+done
+```
+
+Each report must say `GREEN` with no failures; the hardening probes that
+apply `browser-profile/user.js` carry only the shipped profile (the browser
+default of `media.peerconnection.enabled` is true and is not injected). Details and
+mutation modes: `tests/live-e2e/mullvad-browser-hardening/README.md`.
+
+**Real-browser hardening / token-failure probe (tracked).** T186
+(`--only descriptor-matrix`, `--only blocked-proxy`) and T188 (`--only
+private-access`) are the real-browser probes for unintended Direct fallback on
+hardening failure, missing or malformed token, closed sidecar and
+private-window access loss. Packet attribution is by calibrated catchers (a
+destination listener, an ordinary-HTTP-proxy listener, a SOCKS impostor and a
+resolver observer that combines `strace` of port-53 sockets with `MOZ_LOG`
+`nsHostResolver`), each with an in-session positive control and a Tor-route
+positive control; an incomplete request is a failure. This is attribution at the
+browser's own sockets, not a host NIC capture: see R-3 below.
+

+# T200: Ship DoH-off and HTTP/3-off in the browser profile; truthful claims
+
+## Context
+
+Constitution III makes non-Direct routes depend on a tested browser profile with DoH, DoT,
+WebRTC and HTTP/3/QUIC disabled, verified out of band at release cadence. The pinned Mullvad
+Browser 153.3.0esr defaults to DoH-only (`network.trr.mode=3`, Mullvad's Quad9 resolver) and
+leaves HTTP/3 enabled. `browser-profile/user.js`, from which the quickstart builds the only
+supported profile, sets neither pref. Falsification of the T155 attempt-4 redteam found:
+
+- `tests/live-e2e/mullvad-browser-hardening/run.sh` Part 1 is RED on a `prefs.js` built only
+  from the shipped template (DoH-off and HTTP/3-off both fail, exit 1).
+- Every T186/T188 probe session injects `network.trr.mode=5` (`probe.py` around `:1435-1446`),
+  which hides the gap.
+- The quickstart (around `:308-309`), the `hardening.js` failure notification (around
+  `:98-101`) and THREAT-MODEL §5.4/§5.5 call the precondition verified at each release.
+  T195 labelled this the "T091 residue", which the constitution limits to drift after
+  verification.
+- Live experiment X1 (pinned browser, template-only profile) showed no onion name reached the
+  resolver, DoH or HTTP/3: Gecko skips those paths for proxied requests. So this is a
+  precondition-compliance and truthfulness defect, not a demonstrated leak.
+
+## Analysis
+
+- Must hold: the shipped template meets the Constitution III browser precondition for DoH and
+  HTTP/3, the release check verifies the template itself, and no document claims more.
+- Gated: `run.sh` Part 1 against a template-only `prefs.js`; extension unit tests.
+- Residue: post-verification drift stays the documented T091 residue.
+
+## Acceptance
+
+1. Tests first: `run.sh` Part 1 runs against a `prefs.js` built only from the shipped
+   `browser-profile/user.js` (plus nothing the template does not carry). Record it RED before
+   the fix with `scripts/test-first-evidence.py`, then GREEN after.
+2. `browser-profile/user.js` sets `network.trr.mode=5` and `network.http.http3.enable=false`

+# T201: Durable STALE_CONFLICT marker: no changed push until recovery
+
+## Context
+
+`STALE_CONFLICT` is terminal only for the running CP process: `GrpcReloadChannel.recordStale`
+keeps it in memory, and data-model §1.8 "Read" lets changed `tokens.yaml` content propose
+`generation + 1` with no conflict condition. After the CP state is restored from an older
+backup and the DP refuses its generation as stale, each further changed `tokens.yaml` load
+plus CP restart reserves the next generation. Enough of them overtake the DP's generation and
+are accepted, carrying any credential the restored file still lists. Falsification ran this
+with the real `TokenLoader` against a model of the DP reload rule (`server.go:114-121`): three
+changed loads after a restore from a backup two generations old re-authorized a revoked token,
+without the explicit rollback procedure. Each step is an operator edit and each refused step
+shows `STALE_CONFLICT`, so this is not an automatic promotion (Constitution II), but it defeats
+T159's must-hold ("the CP never promotes rejected stale credential content to a newer
+generation") and the quickstart and THREAT-MODEL §5.15 do not warn about it.
+
+## Analysis
+
+- Must hold: once the DP refuses a candidate as stale, the CP durably records the conflict and
+  makes no `ReloadTokens` push of changed content, and none can be accepted, until the
+  documented stale-conflict recovery clears the marker; restarts do not clear it.
+- Gated: CP unit tests (TokenLoader, GrpcReloadChannel), persistence migration test.
+- Residue: host/root rollback of all trusted state stays outside the guarantee (Constitution II).
+
+## Acceptance
+
+1. Tests first: a TokenLoader/GrpcReloadChannel regression with restored-backup state, a stale
+   reply, then N changed loads and a CP restart, in which no push is accepted (or none is made)
+   until the recovery procedure clears the marker. Record RED on the current code with
+   `scripts/test-first-evidence.py` (the falsifier's E4 probe is the reference red), then GREEN.
+2. The CP persists the stale conflict durably (its SQLite state; a migration if needed) and
+   consults it before any changed-content push, across restarts. Recovery option 1 (restore
+   the newer CP state) and option 2 (explicit, operator-confirmed rollback) clear it as the
+   quickstart describes; nothing else does.
+3. `scripts/stargate status` keeps reporting `STALE_CONFLICT` while the marker is set (existing
+   vocabulary; no history, timestamp or label recorded).
+4. Update data-model §1.8, quickstart §"Stale-conflict recovery" and THREAT-MODEL §5.15 to
+   match. THREAT-MODEL wording needs maintainer approval at T201 time: stop and return drafts
+   before writing it.

+// --- resume: session tickets across a peer-pin rotation (T155 A-1) ---------
+
+// countingCache wraps the client session cache and counts lookups that return
+// a stored session, i.e. handshakes in which this client offered a ticket.
+type countingCache struct {
+	tls.ClientSessionCache
+	mu     sync.Mutex
+	offers int
+}
+
+func (c *countingCache) Get(key string) (*tls.ClientSessionState, bool) {
+	session, ok := c.ClientSessionCache.Get(key)
+	if ok && session != nil {
+		c.mu.Lock()
+		c.offers++
+		c.mu.Unlock()
+	}
+	return session, ok
+}
+
+func (c *countingCache) offered() int {
+	c.mu.Lock()
+	defer c.mu.Unlock()
+	return c.offers
+}
+
+// handshakeRecord is what the client saw of one TLS handshake.
+type handshakeRecord struct {
+	resumed bool
+	err     error
+}
+
+// recordingCreds records every client handshake gRPC performs, so a result
+// can name whether the server resumed the offered session.
+type recordingCreds struct {
+	credentials.TransportCredentials
+	mu  *sync.Mutex
+	log *[]handshakeRecord
+}
+
+func (r recordingCreds) ClientHandshake(ctx context.Context, authority string, raw net.Conn) (net.Conn, credentials.AuthInfo, error) {
+	conn, info, err := r.TransportCredentials.ClientHandshake(ctx, authority, raw)
+	rec := handshakeRecord{err: err}
+	if tlsInfo, ok := info.(credentials.TLSInfo); ok {
+		rec.resumed = tlsInfo.State.DidResume
+	}
+	r.mu.Lock()
+	*r.log = append(*r.log, rec)
+	r.mu.Unlock()
+	return conn, info, err
+}
+
+func (r recordingCreds) Clone() credentials.TransportCredentials {
+	return recordingCreds{TransportCredentials: r.TransportCredentials.Clone(), mu: r.mu, log: r.log}
+}
+
+// resumeAttempt is one fresh gRPC connection (one TLS handshake) and one
+// GetStatus with correct §5 metadata.
+type resumeAttempt struct {
+	handshakes []handshakeRecord
+	offered    bool  // the client offered a cached ticket
+	rpcErr     error // nil: the DP accepted the peer and answered
+}
+
+func (a resumeAttempt) String() string {
+	first := "none"
+	if len(a.handshakes) > 0 {
+		first = fmt.Sprintf("resumed=%v", a.handshakes[0].resumed)
+		if a.handshakes[0].err != nil {
+			first = "failed: " + a.handshakes[0].err.Error()
+		}
+	}
+	rpc := "answered"
+	if a.rpcErr != nil {
+		rpc = "refused: " + status.Code(a.rpcErr).String()
+	}
+	return fmt.Sprintf("ticket_offered=%v handshakes=%d first_handshake=[%s] rpc=%s", a.offered, len(a.handshakes), first, rpc)
+}
+
+func attemptStatus(socket, keysDir string, cert tls.Certificate, cache *countingCache, d time.Duration) resumeAttempt {
+	cfg := clientConfig(cert, keysDir+"/dp.pub")
+	// The client verifier must also hold on resumption (the DP's dp.pub is
+	// not rotated here; VerifyPeerCertificate alone would be skipped).
+	cfg.VerifyPeerCertificate = nil
+	pin := pinVerifier(keysDir + "/dp.pub")
+	cfg.VerifyConnection = func(state tls.ConnectionState) error {
+		raw := make([][]byte, 0, len(state.PeerCertificates))
+		for _, cert := range state.PeerCertificates {
+			raw = append(raw, cert.Raw)
+		}
+		return pin(raw, nil)
+	}
+	// A fixed ServerName keys the session cache, so every attempt with the
+	// same cache looks up the same ticket.
+	cfg.ServerName = "stargate-dp"
+	before := 0
+	if cache != nil {
+		cfg.ClientSessionCache = cache
+		before = cache.offered()
+	}
+	var mu sync.Mutex
+	var log []handshakeRecord
+	creds := recordingCreds{TransportCredentials: credentials.NewTLS(cfg), mu: &mu, log: &log}
+	conn, err := grpc.NewClient("unix://"+socket, grpc.WithTransportCredentials(creds))
+	if err != nil {
+		return resumeAttempt{rpcErr: err}
+	}
+	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), d)
+	_, rpcErr := getStatus(ctx, grpcpb.NewControlClient(conn), "1", "0")
+	cancel()
+	_ = conn.Close()
+	mu.Lock()
+	defer mu.Unlock()
+	return resumeAttempt{handshakes: append([]handshakeRecord(nil), log...), offered: cache != nil && cache.offered() > before, rpcErr: rpcErr}
+}

+// probeResume is T155's live A-1 check (wire-auth.md §2.4 "Revocation/
+// rotation"; Constitution II: identity rotation cannot become an auth bypass).
+// The Go DP keeps TLS 1.3 resumption and must re-check the CURRENT cp.pub on a
+// resumed handshake (VerifyConnection, T135). The sequence:
+//
+//  1. old CP identity, full handshake, GetStatus answered (a ticket is issued);
+//  2. same identity and cache: the DP resumed the session and answered.
+//     Positive control: the live DP issues and accepts tickets, so a refusal
+//     in step 4 is the pin check, not missing resumption;
+//  3. rotate cp.priv/cp.pub in place (§6.2; the CP must be stopped);
+//  4. old identity offers the step-1 ticket: no RPC may be answered, and the
+//     handshake must show the resumed path (not a declined ticket). A DP that
+//     skipped the pin check on resumed handshakes (VerifyPeerCertificate only,
+//     the T135 defect) answers it, so this step is the falsifier;
+//  5. old identity, no cache (full handshake): no RPC may be answered;
+//  6. rotated identity, full handshake: answered (the DP re-read the pin and
+//     is serving, so steps 4-5 are refusals, not an outage).
+func probeResume(socket, keysDir string, d time.Duration) error {
+	oldPriv, err := loadSigner(keysDir + "/cp.priv")
+	if err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	oldCert, err := selfSigned(oldPriv, "stargate-cp")
+	if err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	cache := &countingCache{ClientSessionCache: tls.NewLRUClientSessionCache(4)}
+	report := func(step string, a resumeAttempt) { fmt.Printf("wireprobe: resume %s: %s\n", step, a) }
+
+	full := attemptStatus(socket, keysDir, oldCert, cache, d)
+	report("1-old-full", full)
+	if full.rpcErr != nil || len(full.handshakes) == 0 || full.handshakes[0].resumed {
+		return fmt.Errorf("step 1: the old identity's full handshake was not answered: %v", full.rpcErr)
+	}
+	resumed := attemptStatus(socket, keysDir, oldCert, cache, d)
+	report("2-old-resumed-before-rotation", resumed)
+	if resumed.rpcErr != nil || !resumed.offered || len(resumed.handshakes) == 0 || !resumed.handshakes[0].resumed {
+		return errors.New("step 2 (positive control): the DP did not resume the offered ticket before rotation; the post-rotation result would not test resumption")
+	}
+	if err := rotateCPKeys(keysDir); err != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("step 3: rotation: %w", err)
+	}
+	fmt.Println("wireprobe: resume 3-rotated: cp.priv/cp.pub replaced")
+	stale := attemptStatus(socket, keysDir, oldCert, cache, d)
+	report("4-old-ticket-after-rotation", stale)
+	if !stale.offered {
+		return errors.New("step 4: the client did not offer the cached ticket; the probe did not exercise resumption")
+	}
+	if stale.rpcErr == nil {
+		return errors.New("step 4: the DP answered the OLD CP identity on a resumed session after rotation — resumption bypassed the current pin (wire-auth.md §2.4, §3.1)")
+	}
+	// A completed, non-resumed handshake means the DP declined the ticket (a
+	// restart or ticket-key change since step 2) and refused a full handshake
+	// instead: that is step 5's property, so step 4 would pass vacuously. The
+	// resumed path shows as an accepted PSK (resumed=true) or an abort before
+	// the client finished (the DP rejects the restored peer before reading the
+	// client's Finished, so the client's write can race the alert).
+	if h := stale.handshakes; len(h) == 0 || (h[0].err == nil && !h[0].resumed) {
+		return errors.New("step 4: the DP did not take the resumed path (ticket declined or no handshake); the refusal does not test resumption")
+	}
+	oldFull := attemptStatus(socket, keysDir, oldCert, nil, d)
+	report("5-old-full-after-rotation", oldFull)
+	if oldFull.rpcErr == nil {
+		return errors.New("step 5: the DP answered the OLD CP identity on a full handshake after rotation")
+	}
+	newPriv, err := loadSigner(keysDir + "/cp.priv")
+	if err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	newCert, err := selfSigned(newPriv, "stargate-cp")
+	if err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	rotated := attemptStatus(socket, keysDir, newCert, nil, d)
+	report("6-rotated-full", rotated)
+	if rotated.rpcErr != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("step 6: the rotated identity was not answered: %v", rotated.rpcErr)
+	}
+	return nil
+}

+func (statusServer) GetStatus(context.Context, *grpcpb.StatusRequest) (*grpcpb.StatusResponse, error) {

+func writePEM(t *testing.T, path, kind string, der []byte, mode os.FileMode) {
+	t.Helper()
+	if err := os.WriteFile(path, pem.EncodeToMemory(&pem.Block{Type: kind, Bytes: der}), mode); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+}
+
+// standInKeys writes cp.priv, cp.pub and dp.pub in the stargate-keys layout
+// and returns the DP's private key.
+func standInKeys(t *testing.T, dir string) ed25519.PrivateKey {
+	t.Helper()
+	cpPub, cpPriv, err := ed25519.GenerateKey(rand.Reader)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	dpPub, dpPriv, err := ed25519.GenerateKey(rand.Reader)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	privDER, err := x509.MarshalPKCS8PrivateKey(cpPriv)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	writePEM(t, filepath.Join(dir, "cp.priv"), "PRIVATE KEY", privDER, 0o600)
+	for name, pub := range map[string]ed25519.PublicKey{"cp.pub": cpPub, "dp.pub": dpPub} {
+		der, err := x509.MarshalPKIXPublicKey(pub)
+		if err != nil {
+			t.Fatal(err)
+		}
+		writePEM(t, filepath.Join(dir, name), "PUBLIC KEY", der, 0o644)
+	}
+	return dpPriv
+}

+// currentCPPin compares the peer key with cp.pub read now, per handshake.
+func currentCPPin(keysDir string, certs []*x509.Certificate) error {
+	if len(certs) != 1 {
+		return errors.New("want exactly one peer certificate")
+	}
+	raw, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(keysDir, "cp.pub"))
+	if err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	block, _ := pem.Decode(raw)
+	if block == nil {
+		return errors.New("cp.pub: no PEM block")
+	}
+	pinned, err := x509.ParsePKIXPublicKey(block.Bytes)
+	if err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	key, ok := certs[0].PublicKey.(ed25519.PublicKey)
+	if !ok || !key.Equal(pinned) {
+		return errors.New("peer key is not the current cp.pub")
+	}
+	return nil

+			// the tickets the cloned server config issued.
+			var key [32]byte
+			if _, err := rand.Read(key[:]); err != nil {
+				t.Fatal(err)
+			}
+			cfg.SetSessionTicketKeys([][32]byte{key})
+			initial, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(keysDir, "cp.pub"))
+			if err != nil {
+				t.Fatal(err)
+			}
+			cfg.UnwrapSession = func(identity []byte, cs tls.ConnectionState) (*tls.SessionState, error) {
+				if now, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(keysDir, "cp.pub")); err != nil || string(now) != string(initial) {
+					return nil, nil // decline: full handshake
+				}
+				return cfg.DecryptTicket(identity, cs)
+			}
+		}
+	case "peercert":
+		cfg.VerifyPeerCertificate = func(rawCerts [][]byte, _ [][]*x509.Certificate) error {
+			certs := make([]*x509.Certificate, 0, len(rawCerts))
+			for _, raw := range rawCerts {
+				c, err := x509.ParseCertificate(raw)
+				if err != nil {
+					return err
+				}
+				certs = append(certs, c)
+			}
+			return currentCPPin(keysDir, certs)
+		}
+	default:
+		t.Fatalf("unknown stand-in mode %q", mode)
+	}
+	lis, err := net.Listen("unix", socket)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	srv := grpc.NewServer(grpc.Creds(credentials.NewTLS(cfg)))
+	grpcpb.RegisterControlServer(srv, statusServer{})
+	go func() { _ = srv.Serve(lis) }()
+	t.Cleanup(srv.Stop)
+}
+
+func TestProbeResumeDiscriminates(t *testing.T) {
+	cases := []struct {
+		mode    string
+		wantErr string // empty: the probe must pass
+	}{
+		{"connection", ""},
+		{"peercert", "step 4"},
+		{"noticket", "step 2 (positive control)"},
+		{"declined", "did not take the resumed path"},
+	}
+	for _, tc := range cases {
+		t.Run(tc.mode, func(t *testing.T) {
+			dir := t.TempDir()
+			keys := filepath.Join(dir, "k")
+			if err := os.Mkdir(keys, 0o700); err != nil {
+				t.Fatal(err)
+			}
+			dpPriv := standInKeys(t, keys)
+			socket := filepath.Join(dir, "dp.sock")
+			serveStandIn(t, socket, keys, tc.mode, dpPriv)
+			err := probeResume(socket, keys, 5*time.Second)
+			switch {
+			case tc.wantErr == "" && err != nil:
+				t.Fatalf("probe failed against a resumption-safe DP stand-in: %v", err)
+			case tc.wantErr != "" && err == nil:
+				t.Fatalf("probe passed against the %q stand-in; want a failure naming %q", tc.mode, tc.wantErr)
+			case tc.wantErr != "" && !strings.Contains(err.Error(), tc.wantErr):
+				t.Fatalf("probe failed for the wrong reason against %q: %v (want %q)", tc.mode, err, tc.wantErr)
+			}
+		})
+	}
+}

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Copyright 2026 The Stargate Authors
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# T155 Acceptance 4: the live-e2e tracker must exist, carry the required
+# sections, name only commands that exist, track the real-browser Direct-fallback
+# probe and the release-cadence checks, and never record an unrun check as PASS
+# (Constitution VII: SKIP is not PASS; workflow.md "Live end-to-end verification").
+set -euo pipefail
+python3 - "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" <<'PY'
+import re
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+root = Path(sys.argv[1])
+readme = root / 'specs/001-tor-route/live-e2e/README.md'
+errors = []
+
+if not readme.is_file():
+    print('FAIL: specs/001-tor-route/live-e2e/README.md is missing (T155 Acceptance 4)',
+          file=sys.stderr)
+    sys.exit(1)
+text = readme.read_text()
+
+
+def need(label, pattern, flags=re.I | re.S):
+    if not re.search(pattern, text, flags):
+        errors.append(f'missing: {label}')
+
+
+# Required content named by Acceptance 4.
+need('prerequisites section', r'^## .*environment.*disposable host', re.I | re.M)
+need('foundation checks table', r'^## 1\. Foundation checks', re.I | re.M)
+need('evidence index with a snapshot hash',
+     r'## Evidence index.*snapshot\.\*\*\s+executable content is commit `[0-9a-f]{40}`')
+need('preserve/reset semantics', r'### Preserve / reset.*reset every run.*preserve across runs')
+need('transport-relevant vs invisible classification',
+     r'transport-relevant \(live only\).*transport-invisible \(stays in contract tests\)')
+need('real-browser hardening/token-failure probe with packet attribution',
+     r'real-browser hardening / token-failure probe.*direct fallback.*packet attribution')
+need('SKIP is never PASS rule', r'never recorded as pass|never pass', re.I)
+for ticket in ('T186', 'T188', 'T034a', 'T034f', 'T070a'):
+    need(f'{ticket} named', rf'\b{ticket}\b')
+need('browser launch / session restore obligation',
+     r'browser launch and session restore.*run before every release')
+# The evidence snapshot must name a real commit, not any 40-hex string.
+snap = re.search(r'executable content is commit `([0-9a-f]{40})`', text, re.I)
+if snap and subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(root), 'cat-file', '-e', snap.group(1) + '^{commit}'],
+                           capture_output=True).returncode != 0:
+    errors.append(f'evidence snapshot {snap.group(1)} is not a commit in this repository')
+decisions = set(re.findall(r'\*\*D-live-(\d+)', text))
+if len(decisions) < 3:
+    errors.append(f'D-live-N decisions log needs at least 3 entries, found {len(decisions)}')
+
+# Every repository path the tracker tells an operator to run must exist.
+for path in sorted(set(re.findall(
+        r'(?:tests/(?:live-e2e|contract|integration)/[\w./-]+\.(?:py|sh|go)|extension/package\.sh|scripts/verify\.sh)',
+        text))):
+    if not (root / path).is_file():
+        errors.append(f'command path does not exist: {path}')
+
+# An unrun release-cadence check must not carry a PASS status, and a check
+# definition row (F-n) is not a result. An R-n row may name PASS only in the
+# exact negation "never recorded as PASS"; any other PASS/PASSED/GREEN/OK, or a
+# "passed"/"green" in any case, in an R-n or F-n row is an error (a nearby "not"
+# elsewhere in the row is no excuse). Lower-case "pass" stays usable as a noun.
+for line in text.splitlines():
+    if not re.match(r'\|\s*[RF]-?\d+\s*\|', line):
+        continue
+    rest = line.replace('never recorded as PASS', '')
+    if re.search(r'\b(PASS|OK)\b', rest) or re.search(r'\b(passed|green)\b', rest, re.I):
+        errors.append(f'check row claims a result: {line[:80]}')
+
+if errors:
+    print('FAIL: live-e2e tracker (T155 Acceptance 4):', file=sys.stderr)
+    for e in errors:
+        print(f'  - {e}', file=sys.stderr)
+    sys.exit(1)
+print('OK: live-e2e tracker sections, commands, probe tracking and no unrun PASS')
+PY

+// and everything else (target, profile, context) equal, and the pair must

+// t155ParallelConnect is t126ParallelConnect with a token per identity (the
+// device axis needs two bearers). Same starting gun, per-dial retry window and

+func t155ParallelConnect(t *testing.T, ctx context.Context, composeFile, envFile string, c0, c1 t155Cred, wait time.Duration) (net.Conn, net.Conn) {
+	t.Helper()
+	type result struct {
+		idx  int
+		conn net.Conn
+		err  error
+	}
+	start := make(chan struct{})
+	results := make(chan result, 2)
+	for i, cred := range []t155Cred{c0, c1} {
+		go func(idx int, cred t155Cred) {
+			<-start
+			wCtx, wCancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, wait)
+			defer wCancel()
+			for {
+				conn, err := t126Connect(wCtx, cred.user, cred.token)
+				if err == nil {
+					results <- result{idx: idx, conn: conn}
+					return
+				}
+				if wCtx.Err() != nil {
+					results <- result{idx: idx, err: err}
+					return
+				}
+				time.Sleep(t126StreamPoll)
+			}
+		}(i, cred)
+	}
+	close(start)
+	var conns [2]net.Conn
+	var errs [2]error
+	for n := 0; n < 2; n++ {
+		r := <-results
+		conns[r.idx], errs[r.idx] = r.conn, r.err
+	}

+		for _, c := range conns {
+			if c != nil {

+			}
+		}
+		t.Fatalf("parallel CONNECT through %s did not establish both streams within %s\n  #0: %s\n  #1: %s\n%s\n%s",

+			t126LogTail(ctx, composeFile, envFile, "stargate-dp", 12),
+			t126LogTail(ctx, composeFile, envFile, "tor", 15))
+	}
+	return conns[0], conns[1]
+}

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+# Copyright 2026 The Stargate Authors
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# T155 — stack phase on the disposable QEMU guest (run as root from the candidate
+# tree). Real `scripts/stargate init` on fresh volumes, then the quickstart
+# operator surface (tokens.yaml + `restart stargate-control` +
+# `scripts/stargate status`) drives Acceptance 2/7 checks against the deployed
+# DP on 127.0.0.1:8881. Synthetic tokens only; nothing secret is printed.
+# Every check is recorded PASS/FAIL; the script exits non-zero on any FAIL.
+#
+# `--only resumption` runs init, the first acknowledged reload and the TLS
+# resumption phase alone. `--only traffic` runs the real-hour GetStatus probe.
+# The default runs all; traffic publication can take a full UTC hour.
+import hashlib
+import json
+import os
+import secrets
+import shutil
+import socket
+import sqlite3
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import time
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ONLY = sys.argv[2] if sys.argv[1:2] == ["--only"] and len(sys.argv) == 3 else None
+if sys.argv[1:] and ONLY not in ("resumption", "traffic"):
+    sys.exit("usage: t155_stack.py [--only resumption|traffic]")
+
+ROOT = Path.cwd()
+COMPOSE = ROOT / "compose/docker-compose.local.yml"
+STAMP = time.strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S", time.gmtime())
+P = "t155-stack"
+EV = ROOT / "target/live-e2e" / f"T155-stack-{STAMP}"
+EV.mkdir(parents=True)
+ENV = os.environ.copy()
+ENV.update(STARGATE_PROJECT=P, STARGATE_COMPOSE_FILE=str(COMPOSE), STARGATE_ENV_DIR=str(EV),
+           STARGATE_ENV_FILE=str(EV / "local.env"), BUILDX_BUILDER=os.environ.get("BUILDX_BUILDER", "t165-native"))
+C = ["docker", "compose", "-p", P, "-f", str(COMPOSE), "--env-file", str(EV / "local.env")]
+RESULTS = []
+TOK = {name: secrets.token_hex(16) for name in ("laptop", "phone", "tablet", "bogus")}
+GIMG = "golang:1.26.3-bookworm@sha256:252599aeb51ad60b83e4d8821802068127c528c707cb7dd7afd93be057c6011c"
+PROBE = ROOT / "target/stargate-wireprobe"
+
+
+def log(msg):
+    print(msg, flush=True)
+
+
+def check(name, ok, detail=""):
+    RESULTS.append({"check": name, "result": "PASS" if ok else "FAIL", "detail": detail})
+    log(f"{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}: {name}{' — ' + detail if detail else ''}")
+    return ok
+
+
+def run(argv, timeout=600, env=None, ok=True):
+    r = subprocess.run(argv, cwd=ROOT, env=env or ENV, text=True, capture_output=True, timeout=timeout)
+    if ok and r.returncode:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"{' '.join(map(str, argv[:6]))} exit {r.returncode}: {r.stderr[-800:]}")
+    return r
+
+
+def vol(name):
+    return Path(run(["docker", "volume", "inspect", "--format", "{{.Mountpoint}}", f"{P}_{name}"]).stdout.strip())
+
+
+def write_tokens(*labels):
+    # Quickstart step: root writes tokens.yaml into the config volume (sudo tee).
+    body = "tokens:\n" + "".join(f"  - label: {l}\n    token: {TOK[l]}\n" for l in labels)
+    (vol("stargate-control-config") / "tokens.yaml").write_text(body)
+
+
+def status():
+    r = run(["bash", "scripts/stargate", "status"], timeout=60, ok=False)
+    # Whole output, not the last line: STALE_CONFLICT is followed by a pointer line.
+    return r.returncode, ["\n".join((r.stdout + r.stderr).strip().splitlines())]
+
+
+def await_status(rc, needle, timeout):
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
+    while True:
+        code, out = status()
+        if code == rc and needle in out[0]:
+            return out[0]
+        if time.monotonic() > deadline:
+            return f"TIMEOUT last rc={code} out={out[0]}"
+        time.sleep(5)

+def recv_exact(conn, n):
+    data = b""
+    while len(data) < n:
+        part = conn.recv(n - len(data))
+        if not part:
+            break
+        data += part
+    return data
+

+def socks_auth(token, site=b"t155-device-profile-normal-example.com"):
+    """Return (state, conn): state is 'ok', 'denied' or 'closed'."""
+    conn = socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", 8881), timeout=10)
+    conn.settimeout(30)
+    conn.sendall(b"\x05\x01\x02")
+    if recv_exact(conn, 2) != b"\x05\x02":
+        conn.close()
+        return "closed", None
+    user = b"sg1:" + hashlib.sha256(site).hexdigest().encode()
+    t = token.encode()
+    conn.sendall(b"\x01" + bytes([len(user)]) + user + bytes([len(t)]) + t)
+    reply = recv_exact(conn, 2)
+    if reply == b"\x01\x00":
+        return "ok", conn
+    conn.close()
+    return ("denied" if reply == b"\x01\xff" else "closed"), None
+
+
+def auth_state(label):
+    try:
+        state, conn = socks_auth(TOK[label])
+        if conn:
+            conn.close()
+        return state
+    except OSError as exc:
+        return f"error:{type(exc).__name__}"
+

+def tor_bytes(label):
+    for attempt in range(3):
+        try:
+            state, conn = socks_auth(TOK[label])
+            if state != "ok":
+                return f"auth {state}"
+            with conn:
+                target = b"example.com"
+                conn.sendall(b"\x05\x01\x00\x03" + bytes([len(target)]) + target + b"\x00\x50")
+                rep = recv_exact(conn, 10)
+                if rep[:2] != b"\x05\x00":
+                    last = f"reply {rep[:2].hex()}"
+                    continue
+                conn.sendall(b"HEAD / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: example.com\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n")
+                head = conn.recv(64)
+                if head.startswith(b"HTTP/"):
+                    return "ok"
+                last = "no HTTP bytes"
+        except OSError as exc:
+            last = f"{type(exc).__name__}"
+        time.sleep(10)
+    return last
+

+def wait_listener(timeout=180):
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
+    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
+        try:
+            with socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", 8881), timeout=3) as c:
+                c.sendall(b"\x05\x01\x02")
+                if recv_exact(c, 2) == b"\x05\x02":
+                    return True
+        except OSError:
+            pass
+        time.sleep(2)
+    return False

+def traffic_publication_phase():
+    """A7 / control-grpc T158: observe the actual DP RPC across real UTC time.
+    CP operational_aggregates are a separate writer and cannot prove this.
+    No clock injection or DP restart is used. Only synthetic traffic is recorded.
+    """
+    build_probe()
+    samples = []
+    published = {}
+    dp_id = run(C + ["ps", "-q", "stargate-dp"]).stdout.strip()
+
+    def identity():
+        return run(["docker", "inspect", "-f", "{{.Id}} {{.State.StartedAt}} {{.State.Pid}}", dp_id]).stdout.strip()
+
+    started = identity()
+
+    def require(name, ok, detail=""):
+        if not check(name, ok, detail):
+            raise RuntimeError(name)
+
+    def sample():
+        before = int(time.time()) // 3600
+        r = run(["docker", "run", "--rm", "--network", "none", "--user", "5101:5100",
+                 "-v", f"{P}_stargate-ipc:/run/stargate:ro",
+                 "-v", f"{P}_stargate-keys:/etc/stargate/keys:ro",
+                 "-v", f"{ROOT}:/src:ro", GIMG, "/src/target/stargate-wireprobe", "counters"], timeout=60)
+        after = int(time.time()) // 3600
+        response = json.loads(r.stdout)
+        rows = response["counters"]
+        values = {}
+        for row in rows:
+            if set(row) != {"route", "hourBucket", "requestCount", "byteCount"} or row["route"] != "TOR":
+                raise RuntimeError("GetStatus returned unexpected counter fields or route")
+            hour = int(row["hourBucket"])
+            if hour in values:
+                raise RuntimeError("GetStatus returned a duplicate hour")
+            values[hour] = (int(row["requestCount"]), int(row["byteCount"]))
+        samples.append({"before_unix_hour": before, "after_unix_hour": after, "counters": rows})
+        (EV / "traffic-publication.json").write_text(json.dumps(
+            {"dp_identity": started, "samples": samples}, indent=2) + "\n")
+        # A sample straddling rollover may contain the newly completed hour.
+        # The repeated same-hour samples below are the active-export falsifier.
+        require("GetStatus excludes active/future traffic hours", all(h < after for h in values),
+                f"sample {len(samples)}; guest UTC hours {before}..{after}; exported {sorted(values)}")
+        require("previously published traffic rows remain immutable",
+                all(values.get(h) == value for h, value in published.items()))
+        published.update(values)
+        require("DP process unchanged during traffic publication", identity() == started)
+        return before, after, values
+
+    def traffic():
+        result = tor_bytes("laptop")
+        require("traffic publication positive control: authenticated Tor destination bytes", result == "ok", result)
+        # tor_bytes closes its tunnel; allow both forwarding pumps to complete
+        # before checking the bucket. The nonzero completed-byte control below
+        # fails if no bytes were booked in the measured hour.
+        time.sleep(2)
+
+    # If setup crosses the hour, restart the observation window on this same DP.
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + 4200
+    while True:
+        hour = int(time.time()) // 3600
+        traffic()
+        private_samples = 0
+        for _ in range(3):
+            before, after, _ = sample()
+            if before == after == hour:
+                private_samples += 1
+            time.sleep(5)
+        if private_samples == 3 and int(time.time()) // 3600 == hour:
+            break
+        if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
+            raise RuntimeError("no complete pre-boundary observation window")
+    require("repeated same-hour GetStatus reads after traffic", private_samples == 3, f"unix hour {hour}")
+    traffic()
+    sample()
+    log(f"traffic publication: waiting for real UTC boundary after unix hour {hour}")
+    while int(time.time()) // 3600 == hour:
+        if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
+            raise RuntimeError("real UTC hour boundary did not arrive within 70 minutes")
+        time.sleep(15)
+        sample()
+    before, after, rows = sample()
+    require("real UTC hour boundary crossed on the running DP", before > hour and after > hour)
+    completed = rows.get(hour)
+    require("nonzero completed TOR traffic row published",
+            completed is not None and completed[0] > 0 and completed[1] > 0,
+            f"unix hour {hour}; request/byte totals {completed}")
+    for _ in range(3):
+        traffic()
+        _, _, rows = sample()
+        require("completed traffic row unchanged after more Tor traffic", rows.get(hour) == completed)
+    require("traffic publication DP identity unchanged across real rollover", identity() == started, started)

+def resumption_phase():
+    """A2 peer-pin rotation/resumption. With the CP stopped (wire-auth.md §6.2
+    rotation order), `wireprobe resume`, as the CP identity, takes a session
+    ticket from the running DP, resumes it (positive control), rotates
+    cp.priv/cp.pub, offers the old ticket, then the old identity in a full
+    handshake, then the rotated identity. Its exit code decides; each step is
+    also recorded so a failure names its step. Afterwards the observer's
+    cp.pub copy is refreshed with init's helper and the CP restarts on the
+    rotated key."""
+    build_probe()
+    dp_id = run(C + ["ps", "-q", "stargate-dp"]).stdout.strip()
+
+    def dp_started():
+        return run(["docker", "inspect", "-f", "{{.State.StartedAt}} {{.State.Pid}}", dp_id]).stdout.strip()
+
+    run(C + ["stop", "stargate-control"])
+    started = dp_started()
+    r = subprocess.run(["docker", "run", "--rm", "--user", "5101:5100", "-v", f"{P}_stargate-ipc:/run/stargate",
+                        "-v", f"{P}_stargate-keys:/etc/stargate/keys", "-v", f"{ROOT}:/src", "-w", "/src", GIMG,
+                        "/src/target/stargate-wireprobe", "resume", "-socket", "/run/stargate/dp.sock"],
+                       capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=600)
+    (EV / "resume.log").write_text(r.stdout + r.stderr)
+    # The ticket must meet the same DP process that issued it.
+    check("DP process unchanged across the resumption probe", dp_started() == started, started)
+    steps = {l.split()[2].rstrip(":"): l for l in r.stdout.splitlines() if l.startswith("wireprobe: resume ")}
+
+    def step(name, *needles):
+        line = steps.get(name, "")
+        return bool(line) and all(n in line for n in needles), line.split(": ", 2)[-1] if line else "step not reached"
+
+    ok, d = step("2-old-resumed-before-rotation", "ticket_offered=true", "resumed=true", "rpc=answered")
+    check("resumption positive control: DP resumed the offered ticket before rotation", ok, d)
+    ok, d = step("4-old-ticket-after-rotation", "ticket_offered=true", "rpc=refused")
+    ok = ok and "first_handshake=[resumed=false]" not in d  # a declined ticket is not the resumed path
+    check("old CP identity offering its pre-rotation ticket gets no RPC answered", ok, d)
+    ok, d = step("5-old-full-after-rotation", "rpc=refused")
+    check("old CP identity refused on a full handshake after rotation", ok, d)
+    ok, d = step("6-rotated-full", "rpc=answered")
+    check("rotated CP identity answered (DP re-read the pin; the refusals are not an outage)", ok, d)
+    check("wireprobe resume exit 0", r.returncode == 0, f"exit {r.returncode} {r.stderr.strip()[-300:]}")
+    # §6.1 ownership/mode of the rotated files, then the §6.2 observer refresh.
+    run(["docker", "run", "--rm", "--user", "0:0", "-v", f"{P}_stargate-keys:/etc/stargate/keys", GIMG, "bash", "-c",
+         "chown 5101:5100 /etc/stargate/keys/cp.priv /etc/stargate/keys/cp.pub && "
+         "chmod 600 /etc/stargate/keys/cp.priv && chmod 644 /etc/stargate/keys/cp.pub"])
+    run(["bash", "-c", '. scripts/lib/compose.sh && refresh_observer_cp_pub "$1" "$2"', "refresh",
+         f"{P}_stargate-keys", f"{P}_stargate-observer-keys"])
+    run(C + ["start", "stargate-control"])
+    s = await_status(0, "ACKNOWLEDGED(", 1200)
+    check("CP restarted on the rotated key: token delivery acknowledged", "ACKNOWLEDGED(" in s, s)

+// --- resume: session tickets across a peer-pin rotation (T155 A-1) ---------
+
+// countingCache wraps the client session cache and counts lookups that return
+// a stored session, i.e. handshakes in which this client offered a ticket.
+type countingCache struct {
+	tls.ClientSessionCache
+	mu     sync.Mutex
+	offers int
+}
+
+func (c *countingCache) Get(key string) (*tls.ClientSessionState, bool) {
+	session, ok := c.ClientSessionCache.Get(key)
+	if ok && session != nil {
+		c.mu.Lock()
+		c.offers++
+		c.mu.Unlock()
+	}
+	return session, ok
+}
+
+func (c *countingCache) offered() int {
+	c.mu.Lock()
+	defer c.mu.Unlock()
+	return c.offers
+}
+
+// handshakeRecord is what the client saw of one TLS handshake.
+type handshakeRecord struct {
+	peerVerified bool
+	resumed      bool
+	err          error
+}
+
+// recordingCreds records every client handshake gRPC performs, so a result
+// can name whether the server resumed the offered session.
+type recordingCreds struct {
+	credentials.TransportCredentials
+	config *tls.Config
+	mu     *sync.Mutex
+	log    *[]handshakeRecord
+}
+
+func (r recordingCreds) ClientHandshake(ctx context.Context, authority string, raw net.Conn) (net.Conn, credentials.AuthInfo, error) {
+	// gRPC discards TLSInfo when Handshake fails. Observe this specific raw
+	// connection after the normal current-DP-pin check, including error paths.
+	// Go 1.26.3 validates selectedIdentity before DidResume; its callback runs
+	// before server Finished, so this witnesses selected PSK, not completed TLS.
+	cfg := r.config.Clone()
+	verify := cfg.VerifyConnection
+	var observed sync.Mutex
+	var rec handshakeRecord
+	cfg.VerifyConnection = func(state tls.ConnectionState) error {
+		if err := verify(state); err != nil {
+			return err
+		}
+		observed.Lock()
+		rec.peerVerified, rec.resumed = true, state.DidResume
+		observed.Unlock()
+		return nil
+	}
+	conn, info, err := credentials.NewTLS(cfg).ClientHandshake(ctx, authority, raw)
+	observed.Lock()
+	rec.err = err
+	r.mu.Lock()
+	*r.log = append(*r.log, rec)
+	r.mu.Unlock()
+	observed.Unlock()
+	return conn, info, err
+}
+
+func (r recordingCreds) Clone() credentials.TransportCredentials {
+	return recordingCreds{TransportCredentials: r.TransportCredentials.Clone(), config: r.config.Clone(), mu: r.mu, log: r.log}
+}
+
+// resumeAttempt is one fresh gRPC connection (one TLS handshake) and one
+// GetStatus with correct §5 metadata.
+type resumeAttempt struct {
+	handshakes []handshakeRecord
+	offered    bool  // the client offered a cached ticket
+	rpcErr     error // nil: the DP accepted the peer and answered
+}
+
+func (a resumeAttempt) String() string {
+	first := "none"
+	if len(a.handshakes) > 0 {
+		first = fmt.Sprintf("pin_verified=%v resumed=%v", a.handshakes[0].peerVerified, a.handshakes[0].resumed)
+		if a.handshakes[0].err != nil {
+			first += " failed: " + a.handshakes[0].err.Error()
+		}
+	}
+	rpc := "answered"
+	if a.rpcErr != nil {
+		rpc = "refused: " + status.Code(a.rpcErr).String()
+	}
+	return fmt.Sprintf("ticket_offered=%v handshakes=%d first_handshake=[%s] rpc=%s", a.offered, len(a.handshakes), first, rpc)
+}
+
+func attemptStatus(socket, keysDir string, cert tls.Certificate, cache *countingCache, d time.Duration) resumeAttempt {
+	cfg := clientConfig(cert, keysDir+"/dp.pub")
+	// The client verifier must also hold on resumption (the DP's dp.pub is
+	// not rotated here; VerifyPeerCertificate alone would be skipped).
+	cfg.VerifyPeerCertificate = nil
+	pin := pinVerifier(keysDir + "/dp.pub")
+	cfg.VerifyConnection = func(state tls.ConnectionState) error {
+		raw := make([][]byte, 0, len(state.PeerCertificates))
+		for _, cert := range state.PeerCertificates {
+			raw = append(raw, cert.Raw)
+		}
+		return pin(raw, nil)
+	}
+	// A fixed ServerName keys the session cache, so every attempt with the
+	// same cache looks up the same ticket.
+	cfg.ServerName = "stargate-dp"
+	before := 0
+	if cache != nil {
+		cfg.ClientSessionCache = cache
+		before = cache.offered()
+	}
+	var mu sync.Mutex
+	var log []handshakeRecord
+	creds := recordingCreds{TransportCredentials: credentials.NewTLS(cfg), config: cfg, mu: &mu, log: &log}
+	conn, err := grpc.NewClient("unix://"+socket, grpc.WithTransportCredentials(creds))
+	if err != nil {
+		return resumeAttempt{rpcErr: err}
+	}
+	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), d)
+	_, rpcErr := getStatus(ctx, grpcpb.NewControlClient(conn), "1", "0")
+	cancel()
+	_ = conn.Close()
+	mu.Lock()
+	defer mu.Unlock()
+	return resumeAttempt{handshakes: append([]handshakeRecord(nil), log...), offered: cache != nil && cache.offered() > before, rpcErr: rpcErr}
+}

+// probeResume is T155's live A-1 check (wire-auth.md §2.4 "Revocation/
+// rotation"; Constitution II: identity rotation cannot become an auth bypass).
+// The Go DP keeps TLS 1.3 resumption and must re-check the CURRENT cp.pub on a
+// resumed handshake (VerifyConnection, T135). The sequence:
+//
+//  1. old CP identity, full handshake, GetStatus answered (a ticket is issued);
+//  2. same identity and cache: the DP resumed the session and answered.
+//     Positive control: the live DP issues and accepts tickets. Step 4 must
+//     independently witness selected PSK; its error does not prove a cause;
+//  3. rotate cp.priv/cp.pub in place (§6.2; the CP must be stopped);
+//  4. old identity offers the step-1 ticket: no RPC may be answered, and the
+//     handshake must show the resumed path (not a declined ticket). A DP that
+//     skipped the pin check on resumed handshakes (VerifyPeerCertificate only,
+//     the T135 defect) answers it, so this step is the falsifier;
+//  5. old identity, no cache (full handshake): no RPC may be answered;
+//  6. rotated identity, full handshake: answered (the DP re-read the pin and
+//     is serving, so steps 4-5 are refusals, not an outage).
+func probeResume(socket, keysDir string, d time.Duration) error {
+	oldPriv, err := loadSigner(keysDir + "/cp.priv")
+	if err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	oldCert, err := selfSigned(oldPriv, "stargate-cp")
+	if err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	cache := &countingCache{ClientSessionCache: tls.NewLRUClientSessionCache(4)}
+	report := func(step string, a resumeAttempt) { fmt.Printf("wireprobe: resume %s: %s\n", step, a) }
+
+	full := attemptStatus(socket, keysDir, oldCert, cache, d)
+	report("1-old-full", full)
+	if full.rpcErr != nil || len(full.handshakes) != 1 || !full.handshakes[0].peerVerified || full.handshakes[0].resumed {
+		return fmt.Errorf("step 1: the old identity's full handshake was not answered: %v", full.rpcErr)
+	}
+	resumed := attemptStatus(socket, keysDir, oldCert, cache, d)
+	report("2-old-resumed-before-rotation", resumed)
+	if resumed.rpcErr != nil || !resumed.offered || len(resumed.handshakes) != 1 || !resumed.handshakes[0].peerVerified || !resumed.handshakes[0].resumed {
+		return errors.New("step 2 (positive control): the DP did not resume the offered ticket before rotation; the post-rotation result would not test resumption")
+	}
+	if err := rotateCPKeys(keysDir); err != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("step 3: rotation: %w", err)
+	}
+	fmt.Println("wireprobe: resume 3-rotated: cp.priv/cp.pub replaced")
+	stale := attemptStatus(socket, keysDir, oldCert, cache, d)
+	report("4-old-ticket-after-rotation", stale)
+	if !stale.offered {
+		return errors.New("step 4: the client did not offer the cached ticket; the probe did not exercise resumption")
+	}
+	if stale.rpcErr == nil {
+		return errors.New("step 4: the DP answered the OLD CP identity on a resumed session after rotation — resumption bypassed the current pin (wire-auth.md §2.4, §3.1)")
+	}
+	// A cached ticket and an error cannot distinguish selected PSK from an
+	// abort or declined ticket. Require this raw attempt's pin-verified witness;
+	// neither prior success nor a later retry supplies it (Constitution VII).
+	if h := stale.handshakes; len(h) != 1 || !h[0].peerVerified || !h[0].resumed {
+		return errors.New("step 4: the DP did not take the resumed path with a current-DP-pin-verified witness (ticket declined, incomplete flight, abort or ambiguous retries); the refusal does not test resumption")
+	}
+	oldFull := attemptStatus(socket, keysDir, oldCert, nil, d)
+	report("5-old-full-after-rotation", oldFull)
+	if oldFull.rpcErr == nil {
+		return errors.New("step 5: the DP answered the OLD CP identity on a full handshake after rotation")
+	}
+	newPriv, err := loadSigner(keysDir + "/cp.priv")
+	if err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	newCert, err := selfSigned(newPriv, "stargate-cp")
+	if err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	rotated := attemptStatus(socket, keysDir, newCert, nil, d)
+	report("6-rotated-full", rotated)
+	if rotated.rpcErr != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("step 6: the rotated identity was not answered: %v", rotated.rpcErr)
+	}
+	return nil
+}

+// Copyright 2026 The Stargate Authors

+
+// Hermetic discrimination test for the `resume` mode (T155 A-1). The live
+// probe runs against the deployed DP; this test shows, without Docker, that
+// its verdict depends on the property it names. A dp.sock stand-in that
+// re-checks the current cp.pub on resumed handshakes (VerifyConnection, as
+// wire-auth.md §3.1/§4 require) must pass; one that pins only on full
+// handshakes (VerifyPeerCertificate, the T135 defect) must fail at step 4;
+// one that never issues tickets must fail the step-2 positive control; one
+// that declines the old ticket after the rotation (as a restarted DP would)
+// must fail step 4 as vacuous, because its refusal is a full handshake.
+// The stand-in's pin check is written here, independently of the probe's.
+package main
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"crypto/ed25519"
+	"crypto/rand"
+	"crypto/tls"
+	"crypto/x509"
+	"encoding/pem"

+)

+type statusServer struct {
+	grpcpb.UnimplementedControlServer
+}
+
+func (statusServer) GetStatus(context.Context, *grpcpb.StatusRequest) (*grpcpb.StatusResponse, error) {
+	return &grpcpb.StatusResponse{}, nil
+}
+
+func writePEM(t *testing.T, path, kind string, der []byte, mode os.FileMode) {
+	t.Helper()
+	if err := os.WriteFile(path, pem.EncodeToMemory(&pem.Block{Type: kind, Bytes: der}), mode); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+}
+
+// standInKeys writes cp.priv, cp.pub and dp.pub in the stargate-keys layout
+// and returns the DP's private key.
+func standInKeys(t *testing.T, dir string) ed25519.PrivateKey {
+	t.Helper()
+	cpPub, cpPriv, err := ed25519.GenerateKey(rand.Reader)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	dpPub, dpPriv, err := ed25519.GenerateKey(rand.Reader)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	privDER, err := x509.MarshalPKCS8PrivateKey(cpPriv)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	writePEM(t, filepath.Join(dir, "cp.priv"), "PRIVATE KEY", privDER, 0o600)
+	for name, pub := range map[string]ed25519.PublicKey{"cp.pub": cpPub, "dp.pub": dpPub} {
+		der, err := x509.MarshalPKIXPublicKey(pub)
+		if err != nil {
+			t.Fatal(err)
+		}
+		writePEM(t, filepath.Join(dir, name), "PUBLIC KEY", der, 0o644)
+	}
+	return dpPriv
+}
+
+// currentCPPin compares the peer key with cp.pub read now, per handshake.
+func currentCPPin(keysDir string, certs []*x509.Certificate) error {
+	if len(certs) != 1 {
+		return errors.New("want exactly one peer certificate")
+	}
+	raw, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(keysDir, "cp.pub"))
+	if err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	block, _ := pem.Decode(raw)
+	if block == nil {
+		return errors.New("cp.pub: no PEM block")
+	}
+	pinned, err := x509.ParsePKIXPublicKey(block.Bytes)
+	if err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	key, ok := certs[0].PublicKey.(ed25519.PublicKey)
+	if !ok || !key.Equal(pinned) {
+		return errors.New("peer key is not the current cp.pub")
+	}
+	return nil
+}

+// serveStandIn starts a dp.sock stand-in. mode is "connection" (pin on full
+// and resumed handshakes), "peercert" (pin on full handshakes only),
+// "noticket" (correct pin, session tickets disabled) or "declined" (correct
+// pin; tickets are refused once cp.pub has changed, like a restarted DP).
+func serveStandIn(t *testing.T, socket, keysDir, mode string, dpPriv ed25519.PrivateKey) {
+	t.Helper()
+	cert, err := selfSigned(dpPriv, "stargate-dp")
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	cfg := &tls.Config{
+		Certificates: []tls.Certificate{cert},
+		ClientAuth:   tls.RequireAnyClientCert,
+		MinVersion:   tls.VersionTLS13,
+	}
+	var partial func(net.Conn) net.Conn
+	switch mode {
+	case "connection", "noticket", "declined", "partialflight":
+		cfg.VerifyConnection = func(state tls.ConnectionState) error {
+			return currentCPPin(keysDir, state.PeerCertificates)
+		}
+		cfg.SessionTicketsDisabled = mode == "noticket"
+		if mode == "declined" || mode == "partialflight" {
+			// Fixed keys survive the credentials' Clone, so cfg can decrypt
+			// the tickets the cloned server config issued.
+			var key [32]byte
+			if _, err := rand.Read(key[:]); err != nil {
+				t.Fatal(err)
+			}
+			cfg.SetSessionTicketKeys([][32]byte{key})
+			initial, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(keysDir, "cp.pub"))
+			if err != nil {
+				t.Fatal(err)
+			}
+			changed := func() bool {
+				now, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(keysDir, "cp.pub"))
+				return err != nil || string(now) != string(initial)
+			}
+			var restored, truncated atomic.Int32
+			var selected atomic.Bool
+			cfg.UnwrapSession = func(identity []byte, cs tls.ConnectionState) (*tls.SessionState, error) {
+				if changed() && mode == "declined" {
+					return nil, nil // decline: full handshake
+				}
+				state, err := cfg.DecryptTicket(identity, cs)
+				if state != nil && changed() {
+					restored.Add(1)
+					selected.Store(true)
+				}
+				return state, err
+			}
+			if mode == "partialflight" {
+				partial = func(c net.Conn) net.Conn {
+					return &partialFlightConn{Conn: c, changed: changed, selected: &selected, truncated: &truncated}
+				}
+				t.Cleanup(func() {
+					if restored.Load() == 0 || truncated.Load() == 0 {
+						t.Errorf("incomplete-flight controls invalid: restored=%d truncated=%d", restored.Load(), truncated.Load())
+					}
+				})
+			}
+		}
+	case "peercert":
+		cfg.VerifyPeerCertificate = func(rawCerts [][]byte, _ [][]*x509.Certificate) error {
+			certs := make([]*x509.Certificate, 0, len(rawCerts))
+			for _, raw := range rawCerts {
+				c, err := x509.ParseCertificate(raw)
+				if err != nil {
+					return err
+				}
+				certs = append(certs, c)
+			}
+			return currentCPPin(keysDir, certs)
+		}
+	default:
+		t.Fatalf("unknown stand-in mode %q", mode)
+	}
+	lis, err := net.Listen("unix", socket)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if partial != nil {
+		lis = wrappingListener{Listener: lis, wrap: partial}
+	}
+	srv := grpc.NewServer(grpc.Creds(credentials.NewTLS(cfg)))
+	grpcpb.RegisterControlServer(srv, statusServer{})
+	go func() { _ = srv.Serve(lis) }()
+	t.Cleanup(srv.Stop)
+}

+func TestProbeResumeDiscriminates(t *testing.T) {
+	cases := []struct {
+		mode    string
+		wantErr string // empty: the probe must pass
+	}{
+		{"connection", ""},
+		{"peercert", "step 4"},
+		{"noticket", "step 2 (positive control)"},
+		{"declined", "did not take the resumed path"},
+		{"partialflight", "did not take the resumed path"},
+	}
+	for _, tc := range cases {
+		t.Run(tc.mode, func(t *testing.T) {
+			dir := t.TempDir()
+			keys := filepath.Join(dir, "k")
+			if err := os.Mkdir(keys, 0o700); err != nil {
+				t.Fatal(err)
+			}
+			dpPriv := standInKeys(t, keys)
+			socket := filepath.Join(dir, "dp.sock")
+			serveStandIn(t, socket, keys, tc.mode, dpPriv)
+			err := probeResume(socket, keys, 5*time.Second)
+			switch {
+			case tc.wantErr == "" && err != nil:
+				t.Fatalf("probe failed against a resumption-safe DP stand-in: %v", err)
+			case tc.wantErr != "" && err == nil:
+				t.Fatalf("probe passed against the %q stand-in; want a failure naming %q", tc.mode, tc.wantErr)
+			case tc.wantErr != "" && !strings.Contains(err.Error(), tc.wantErr):
+				t.Fatalf("probe failed for the wrong reason against %q: %v (want %q)", tc.mode, err, tc.wantErr)
+			}
+		})
+	}
+	t.Run("HandshakeWitnessAttribution", testHandshakeWitnessAttribution)
+}
